newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks get boost from U.S. long bond in morning.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks get boost from U.S. long bond in morning.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks began Monday's session with solid gains as a decline in the U.S. long bond yield gave prices a lift, traders said.
"I think people are reacting to the movement of the bond market. There is some buying around and more importantly there is no selling," said James Osborn, sales director at ING Barings.
The Hang Seng index was up 118 points at 13,512. Turnover was HK$1.07 billion.
On Friday, the U.S. long bond rose 31/32, bringing the yield down to its lowest level since March 4 at 6.36 percent.

Boby Ho, dealing manager at GK Goh Securities, said stocks were also benefiting from a continued recovery after last Thursday's slide of 220 points. "The market is seeing some of the technical rebound continuing from last Friday," he said.
The Hang Seng rose 83.17 points on Friday.

Osborn said although the market had been rising rapidly, leading to calls for consolidation, investors were unwilling to take profits. "The market is in a status quo - it is fairly valued but has moved a long way. People are not going to take profit to move elsewhere because elsewhere does not look particularly attractive," he said.
Osborn said the Hang Seng would either fall back to 13,000 points this week or test a new high at 13,800 points.
"I still predict 13,800 this week," Osborn said.
But Ho said the index would only hit a new high if turnover increased.

"I would think maybe it will come off later this week with some sort of profit-taking but I think it is too early to say," he said. "With (daily) turnover of HK$7-8 billion, I don't think the market will test a new high this week."
He said interest was likely to spread to second liner stocks with RNA Holdings making a strong stock market debut on Monday.
"Maybe some second liners could be active partly because of the new issue today, RNA Holdings, which has opened pretty well," said Ho.
Shares in the company, a spin-off of bullion and jewellery trader Tem Fat Hing Fung, opened at HK$1.32 per share compared with an issue price of HK$1.01.
Property stocks continued strong with Cheung Kong advancing HK$1.00 to HK$69.00, Sun Hung Kai Properties up HK$1.00 at HK$97.00 and Henderson Land up HK$1.00 to HK$78.75.
HSBC Holdings was up HK$1.50 at HK$162.50.
